item.title: Three dead in hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship
item.description: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a polar cruise ship sailing the Atlantic Ocean has killed at least three people and left a fourth in intensive care, prompting an international public health response led by the World Health Organization.

item.title: Trump launches 'Project Freedom' to escort ships from Hormuz
item.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that the U.S. Navy will begin escorting neutral foreign vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday morning under an initiative he called "Project Freedom," framing the operation as a humanitarian mission amid increasingly dire conditions for tens of thousands of sailors trapped in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Cargo ship attacked near Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall
item.description:
A bulk carrier near the Strait of Hormuz reported being attacked by multiple small craft on Sunday, according to the British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center, marking at least the 24th attack in and around the vital waterway since the Iran war began in late February.

The UKMTO said the northbound vessel was attacked 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran, east of the strait, and that all crew were safe. No one immediately claimed responsibility for the incident, the first reported in the area since April 22. The threat level in the region remains classified as critical.

item.title: Starmer, Zelenskyy meet in Yerevan as UK seeks to join EU's Ukraine loan program
item.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrived in Yerevan, Armenia, on Sunday ahead of the 8th European Political Community summit, where he is expected to press for the United Kingdom's participation in the European Union's €90 billion loan program for Ukraine. The move marks a further step in London's post-Brexit rapprochement with Brussels, driven by shared concerns over the war in Ukraine and shifting transatlantic dynamics under the Trump administration.

item.title: NATO's Rutte says Europeans 'got the message' on Iran war
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte declared on Monday that European nations have "gotten the message" from U.S. President Donald Trump over their reluctance to back the ongoing U.S.-led war against Iran, as the transatlantic rift over the conflict deepened following Washington's decision to withdraw thousands of troops from Germany.

item.title: Iran vows to attack US forces as Project Freedom launches in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday announced a naval operation called "Project Freedom" to guide stranded commercial ships through the blocked Strait of Hormuz, setting up a direct confrontation with Iran, which warned it would attack any foreign military force entering the waterway.

The operation, revealed in a Truth Social post, is set to begin Monday morning Middle East time. Trump described the stranded vessels as belonging to countries that are "neutral and innocent bystanders" with no involvement in the broader Middle East conflict. "For the good of Iran, the Middle East, and the United States, we have told these Countries that we will guide their Ships safely out of these restricted Waterways," Trump wrote.

item.title: Iran fires missiles at US warship as Project Freedom launches
item.description:
Two Iranian missiles struck a U.S. warship near Iran's Jask Island on Monday after the vessel reportedly ignored Iranian warnings while attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz, according to IRGC-affiliated Fars News. The reported strike came just hours after U.S. Central Command began Project Freedom, the American military operation to escort stranded commercial vessels through the contested waterway.

Oil prices surged on the news, reflecting the market's acute sensitivity to military confrontations in the corridor through which roughly a quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade passes. Brent crude had already been trading above $116 per barrel heading into the week.

item.title: Two US-flagged ships transit Hormuz under Project Freedom
item.description:
Two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday under the Trump administration's "Project Freedom" initiative, marking the first publicly acknowledged American-backed passage through the strategic waterway since Iran imposed a blockade more than two months ago.

"American forces are actively assisting efforts to restore transit for commercial shipping. As a first step, two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz and are safely headed on their journey," U.S. Central Command said in a post on X.

CENTCOM confirmed that U.S. Navy guided-missile destroyers entered the Arabian Gulf after transiting the strait in support of the operation. The mission involves approximately 15,000 service members, more than 100 land- and sea-based aircraft, and unmanned platforms across multiple domains.

item.title: CENTCOM denies Iran's claim of missile strike as Hormuz operation begins
item.description: Iran said on Monday that it struck a U.S. Navy frigate with two missiles near the Strait of Hormuz, a claim swiftly denied by the U.S. military as President Donald Trump's high-stakes naval operation to reopen the waterway got underway. The dueling narratives underscored the volatility of a standoff that has choked off roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments for more than two months.

item.title: Trump's 'Project Freedom' launches with few details, leaving shippers scrambling
item.description: President Donald Trump on Sunday announced "Project Freedom," a plan to help commercial vessels trapped in the Persian Gulf navigate safely through the Strait of Hormuz, but the initiative went live on Monday with few operational details and no coordination with the shipping industry it aims to serve.

item.title: UAE issues missile alert as Hormuz standoff intensifies
item.description:
Residents in the United Arab Emirates received emergency mobile alerts on Monday warning of a potential missile threat, as explosions from air defense intercepts were heard over Dubai. The National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority (NCEMA) urged people to shelter in place and follow official channels, before issuing a follow-up message declaring the situation safe.

The incident marks the first such alert since the US-Iran ceasefire was declared on April 8, and comes as tensions in the region have escalated sharply following President Donald Trump's announcement of "Project Freedom," a naval operation to guide stranded vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran threatens to attack ships as U.S. launches Project Freedom
item.description:
Oil prices rose sharply on Monday as Iran warned it would target any vessel attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz without its authorization, escalating a confrontation with the United States over the critical waterway that has been effectively shut since the start of the U.S.-Iran war in late February.

Brent crude climbed more than 3 percent to around $112 per barrel and briefly topped $114 during the session, while West Texas Intermediate crude gained nearly 3 percent to approximately $105 per barrel, according to the Associated Press. The surge came as Iran directly challenged President Donald Trump's newly announced "Project Freedom," a military operation to escort stranded commercial ships out of the strait.

item.title: UAE air defenses engage Iranian missiles and drones
item.description: The United Arab Emirates issued a brief emergency alert on Sunday warning residents of potential missile threats, before later declaring the situation safe, as Iranian strikes on Gulf targets entered a new phase amid a wider confrontation between Tehran and Washington over the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Putin retreating to bunkers amid coup and drone fears, EU intelligence report says
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has been spending extended periods in underground bunkers in southern Russia since March 2026, gripped by fears of both a coup by political elites and a drone-based assassination, according to reports published by the Financial Times and the independent Russian investigative outlet Istories (Important Stories), citing a classified European intelligence report.

The revelations came as a Ukrainian drone struck a 52-story luxury residential tower on Mosfilmovskaya Street in Moscow overnight on May 4 — roughly six kilometers from the Kremlin — underscoring the aerial threats that have rattled the Russian leadership. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin confirmed the strike on Telegram, saying there were no casualties. The attack occurred just five days before Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade, for which the defense ministry had already announced that military equipment and cadets would be absent from Red Square this year as a precaution against drone strikes.

item.title: Trump urges South Korea to join Hormuz mission after ship attack
item.description: President Donald Trump has called on South Korea to participate in "Project Freedom," the U.S.-led naval operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing an attack on a South Korean cargo ship as grounds for Seoul's involvement. The renewed pressure on Monday came as the United States launched its effort to guide stranded commercial vessels through the contested waterway, escalating a months-long diplomatic push to draw allies into the Middle East conflict with Iran.

item.title: Russia formally declares May 8-9 ceasefire in Ukraine for Victory Day
item.description: Russia's Defence Ministry announced on Monday that President Vladimir Putin has ordered a ceasefire in Ukraine on May 8-9 to mark the anniversary of the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two. The declaration formalizes a proposal Putin first floated during a 90-minute phone call with U.S. President Donald Trump on April 29.

item.title: Zelensky declares Ukraine ceasefire starting May 5-6
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Monday that Ukraine will observe a unilateral ceasefire beginning at midnight on the night of May 5-6, moving ahead without a formal agreement from Moscow. Writing on Telegram, Zelensky stated that Ukraine is proceeding because "human life is incomparably more valuable than the celebration of any anniversary," and that Ukraine will "act symmetrically" from the moment the ceasefire takes effect — echoing language he used during Ukraine's observance of an Orthodox Easter truce in April.

The announcement comes hours after Russia's Defense Ministry declared its own two-day ceasefire for May 8-9 to coincide with the 81st anniversary of Victory Day, which commemorates the Soviet Union's defeat of Nazi Germany. The Kremlin said it did not require Ukraine's consent and threatened a "massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv" if Ukrainian forces attempted to disrupt the celebrations.

item.title: Iran's nuclear timeline unchanged despite war, US intel finds
item.description: Two months into a U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments indicate that the time Tehran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not shifted since last summer, when a joint U.S.-Israeli strike extended the timeline to roughly nine months to a year, Reuters reported on Monday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Pentagon says Iran attacks on US forces 'below threshold' to restart war
item.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Tuesday that the US-Iran ceasefire remains intact despite a sharp escalation of hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, telling reporters at a Pentagon press briefing that "the ceasefire is not over" even as Iran has attacked American forces more than 10 times since the truce began on April 7.

Gen. Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said the attacks remain "below the threshold for recommencing significant combat operations," adding that Iran has also fired on commercial vessels nine times and seized two container ships during the ceasefire period. "The decision to restart operations is a political one beyond my authority," Caine said. "Currently, what we are experiencing is minor harassing fire. It seems as though Iran is clutching at straws".

item.title: US military confirms loss of KC-135 tanker over Persian Gulf
item.description: A US Air Force KC-135 Stratotanker vanished from radar over the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday after broadcasting a 7700 emergency distress signal, raising alarm on the second day of Operation Project Freedom, the American military operation to guide commercial ships through the contested waterway.
